title: Affine-Layer Density for Exponential Degree Growth
summary: The design seeks exponential algebraic-degree growth with low-degree S-boxes and low FHE overhead; the required affine-layer density remains to be characterized.

formal_statement.body: In the Chaghri-related component design, determine analytically, or by a more refined method, how dense the affine layer must be to obtain exponential algebraic-degree growth while retaining the low-degree S-box and low-FHE-overhead design conditions. The unresolved task is to characterize the required affine-layer density for that degree-growth objective; the supplied context does not specify a particular density measure.

scope.domain: Design of Chaghri-related symmetric-cryptographic components with controlled algebraic-degree growth.
assumptions: The design retains a low-degree S-box.
The design retains low FHE overhead.
parameters: Affine-layer density, governing the targeted exponential algebraic-degree growth
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine analytically, or through a more refined method, how dense the affine layer must be to achieve exponential algebraic-degree growth.

citations.label: Coefficient Grouping: Breaking Chaghri and More

progress.summary: The paper explicitly lists this question among its open questions. It asks for a refined or analytical characterization of the affine-layer density needed for exponential degree growth.
